newsitem.title: UK: IBCA affirms Tesco l-term, s-term ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA affirms Tesco l-term, s-term ratings.

text.p: London, March 21 - IBCA, the European credit rating agency, has affirmed the long-term and short-term ratings for Tesco PLC of AA- and A1+.
This follows the agreement entered into today by Tesco to acquire the food retailing and related businesses of Associated British Foods plc (ABF) in Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.
The acquisition is subject to European Commission approval.

Tesco is acquiring: - 75 stores trading as Quinnsworth and Crazy Prices in the Republic of Ireland; - 34 stores trading as Stewarts, Crazy Prices, Superdeal, Westside Stores and Bloomfields in Northern Ireland; - Kingsway Fresh Food and Dailywrap Produce, pork processors and produce sourcing and packaging businesses respectively in Northern Ireland; - Wine Barrel, a chain of 79 off licences, and Lifestyle Sports and Leisure, a chain of 47 retail sports shops, in the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland.
Total turnover of these businesses was GBP1,224 million in the year to September 14 1996 and operating profits were GBP58 million.

The proposed acquisition constitutes sound business sense in that Tesco is buying businesses in both food and other areas of retailing that it is familiar with. The acquisition cost is GBP630 million and net asset value of the acquired businesses is GBP170 million.

Gearing is expected to rise as a result of the acquisition, and should be around 35%. Today's announced purchase will be wholly debt financed, and the operating profits acquired are expected to cover additional interest expense, suggesting that coverages will not come under significant pressure.
On the grounds that the acquisition is in Tesco's direct area of activity and that the incremental financial risk is limited, IBCA is affirming Tesco's ratings.
